newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber end up on pre-weekend shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber end up on pre-weekend shortcovering.

text.p: Shortcovering ahead of the weekend continued to support CME lumber futures despite the continued weak undertone to cash, traders said.
Lumber closed $4.20 to $2.50 higher, with May up most at $363.70 per tbf and July up $3.40 at $360.90 per tbf.
Shortcovering developed because futures held a discount to cash and this keep the market supported in light dealings. But a persistent weak undertone to cash markets limited gains, they said.
Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $372 per tbf, down $5 from midweek and week ago levels.
